definition: A tendency for evaluators (human or AI) to favor longer responses, independent of their actual quality or correctness.
details: Length bias is a recognized confound in both human evaluation and LLM-as-a-judge setups, motivating evaluation methodologies that explicitly control for or normalize against response length.

explainer.lead: Length bias is the tendency for evaluators, whether human or AI, to favor longer responses regardless of their actual quality or correctness. It matters because it can distort evaluation results and model rankings.

tiers.eli5: It's like a teacher giving higher marks to the longer essay even when the short one answers the question better.
tiers.practitioner: It is a recognized confound in both human evaluation and LLM-as-a-judge setups, so engineers should explicitly control for or normalize against response length. A pitfall is treating longer outputs as higher quality by default.
tiers.paperLevel: A tendency for evaluators (human or AI) to favor longer responses independent of quality or correctness; mitigated by evaluation methodologies that control for or normalize against response length.

explainer.example: In an LLM-as-a-judge comparison, a verbose but vague answer is scored above a concise correct one; normalizing scores against response length exposes the bias.
